name: Error Handler - Log Failures to Administrate

nodes.name: Extract failure
nodes.notes: The Error Trigger payload is metadata only. This normalises it and nothing more.

nodes.name: Fetch failed execution
nodes.notes: Best effort. If this fails the handler still logs what the trigger gave it, because an error handler that throws is the one failure nobody ever sees.

nodes.name: Build failure record
nodes.notes: Splits the failure in two: plain language for Administrate, full detail for the data table.

nodes.name: Record the failure
nodes.notes: The durable record. n8n executions are pruned and Administrate log entries cannot be filtered by origin, so this is the only queryable history of failures.

nodes.notes: Run-level entry, filed under the Organisation type because a dead run has no single affected record. Keeps to plain language on purpose.

parameters.content:
## Error Handler - Log Failures to Administrate (shared)

Set as the **Error Workflow** on any workflow you want covered (Workflow settings > Error workflow). It is not called directly and never appears on the calling workflow's canvas. It catches a run that **dies**.

### The two layers are not redundant

Well-built workflows already check the errors arrays behind every Administrate mutation, because Administrate refuses a mutation inside an HTTP 200. That handles a refusal and keeps the run going.

This catches the other thing: the run that stops. A failed query, a refused HTTP call, a Stop and Error. Nothing downstream of those ever runs, so nothing downstream can report them. You need both layers.

### It writes the failure twice, on purpose

**To the Administrate integration log**, in plain language: what failed, why, when. Nothing else. The failed node, run mode and stack are n8n internals and are kept out of a log that Administrate users read.

**To the `automation_failures` Data Table**, in full. n8n prunes executions, and `ExternalLog` does not expose `originIdentifier` on read, so Administrate cannot be asked for "every failure from this automation". The table is the queryable history.

### Nothing here should throw

The external calls continue on error. A handler that fails produces the one failure nobody ever hears about.

## Config Explained

**ADM_GRAPHQL_URL** - the Administrate API address. The same for every instance; which instance you reach is decided by the credential.

**ADM_LOG_ORIGIN_IDENTIFIER** - the origin name on every failure entry, so failures are distinguishable from the entries your other workflows write. Administrate will not let you filter by it on read; that is what the Data Table is for.

**ADM_RUN_LEVEL_NODE_ID** - a base64 type sentinel, not a record id. `T3JnYW5pc2F0aW9uOg==` decodes to `Organisation:`, and an entry sent with it files under that entity type rather than against one record. A dead run has no single affected record, which is why this exists. `UGVyc29uOg==` is the Contact equivalent if you prefer.

**N8N_API_BASE_URL** - your n8n public API base (`https://YOUR-N8N-HOST/api/v1`). The failed execution is fetched back from here, because the Error Trigger payload carries only metadata.

**N8N_UI_BASE_URL** - your n8n base URL (`https://YOUR-N8N-HOST`), used to build the link to the failed execution. The link in the trigger payload is not used because it can read `localhost:5678`.

**FAILURES_TABLE_ID** - the id of your `automation_failures` Data Table. **Record the failure** reads it by expression; do not re-select the table in the node.

Replace `YOUR-N8N-HOST` in both URLs. If they point at the wrong n8n, the fetch-back silently returns nothing and every execution link is wrong.

## Adding a notification (optional)

This handler logs; it does not send. To add an alert, add an IF reading a `NOTIFY_ENABLED` value in Config and a channel node (email, Slack, Teams) on its true branch, wired between **Log failure to Administrate** and **Done**. The text is already built: **Build failure record** emits `notify_subject` and `notify_body`. Update the `notified` column in **Record the failure** to match.

nodes.name: Sticky - How to Attach and Test

parameters.content:
## Attaching this to a workflow

Open the workflow you want covered, then **Workflow settings > Error workflow** and select this workflow. Save.

Do not also put an Error Trigger inside that workflow itself. Where both exist the Error Workflow wins, and the inline one becomes dead code that looks live.

## Testing it

**An Error Workflow fires on production runs only.** A manual execution never reaches it, however broken the workflow is.

To prove it, build a throwaway workflow with this set as its Error Workflow, run it in production mode (for example on a schedule or a webhook), ending in a Stop and Error node. Then check for a new row in `automation_failures` and a `failed` entry in the Administrate integration log under the Organisation type.

## Republish after every change

Editing this while it is published diverges the draft from the live version, and the live version is the one that answers when something fails.
